title: Scaling AI Systems — Schedule Uneven Requests
key_insight: Schedulers can group compatible lengths, preempt low-priority work, and continuously batch tokens from active requests.
body:
## Schedule Uneven Requests

Short prompts wait behind huge generations, wasting user patience and accelerator slots. Request count alone hides the work size.

Schedulers can group compatible lengths, preempt low-priority work, and continuously batch tokens from active requests.

Set tenant quotas and priority classes using compute estimates. Fairness means sharing scarce work capacity, not giving identical counts of unequal requests.
common_mistakes: Adding random servers always removes the bottleneck.
Every AI request consumes equal compute.
Average traffic alone proves burst capacity.
mini_exercise: Draw “Schedule Uneven Requests” as three labeled steps, then explain the decision at each step.
real_world_usage: AI workloads combine bursty requests, large inputs, expensive inference, and shared capacity.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Schedule Uneven Requests,” explain Scaling AI Systems without assuming the listener knows AI engineering.
